note: Bart 11-11: places, animals and props of Babylon and the new farmers (vault topics/babylon-new-farmers).

sheets.subject: Southern Mesopotamia c. 1750 BCE, the dry steppe west of the Euphrates and the farmland near Babylon: the dry rolling steppe at dawn: low bare hills, sparse dry grass and a few thorny shrubs, wide empty land, far away a thin line of green where the river is.
The dry steppe: pale dusty earth, sparse tufts of dry grass, small stones and a few low thorny shrubs
The dry steppe: pale dusty earth, sparse tufts of dry grass, small stones and a few low thorny shrubs

Southern Mesopotamia c. 1750 BCE, the dry steppe west of the Euphrates and the farmland near Babylon: the river bank at dusk seen from the land: a dense thicket of tamarisk trees and tall reeds along the river, the water glinting between them, the far bank low and flat.

Southern Mesopotamia c. 1750 BCE, the dry steppe west of the Euphrates and the farmland near Babylon: (1) one tamarisk tree, 6 m high, gnarled trunk, feathery grey-green foliage, a strong low branch about 2.5 m up that a man could sit on; (2) a dense clump of tall river reeds, 3 m high.
A river bank at dusk: dark damp earth and mud, tufts of reeds, small pools, fallen leaves of tamarisk
A river bank at dusk: dark damp earth and mud, tufts of reeds, small pools, fallen leaves of tamarisk

Southern Mesopotamia c. 1750 BCE, the dry steppe west of the Euphrates and the farmland near Babylon: a semi-nomadic herders camp: (1) a low tent of dark woven goat hair stretched over wooden poles, open at the front, 2.2 m high; (2) a second smaller tent, 1.8 m high; (3) a ring of stones with a small fire of dry sticks, 0.6 m high with its flames; (4) a pen of thorny branches for goats, 1 m high.

Southern Mesopotamia c. 1750 BCE, the dry steppe west of the Euphrates and the farmland near Babylon: animals, each a separate full-body animal in side view: (1) a lion of Mesopotamia, a big male with a dark short mane, prowling low and tense, 1.1 m at the shoulder; (2) the same kind of lion slinking away with its head turned back; (3) a horse tethered by a rope, ears back, nervous, 1.5 m at the shoulder, no saddle; (4) a donkey carrying two packs, 1.1 m.

Southern Mesopotamia c. 1750 BCE, the dry steppe west of the Euphrates and the farmland near Babylon: animals, each a separate full-body animal: (1) a thin brown goat grazing, head down; (2) a black goat standing, looking up; (3) a white goat lying down; (4) two oxen side by side under a wooden yoke pulling a wooden seeder plow with a funnel on top, the plow included, 1.5 m high, 3.5 m long.

Southern Mesopotamia c. 1750 BCE, the dry steppe west of the Euphrates and the farmland near Babylon: six separate objects: (1) a shallow clay milk bowl, 0.2 m wide; (2) a cloth food bundle tied with cord, 0.3 m; (3) a fat woven bag of barley seed, 0.5 m; (4) two tied barley sheaves leaning together, 0.9 m; (5) a stack of sun-dried mud bricks, 0.6 m; (6) a broken wooden spear in two pieces, 1.4 m.

Southern Mesopotamia c. 1750 BCE, the dry steppe west of the Euphrates and the farmland near Babylon: (1) a dry old riverbed seen across from the side: a shallow hollow with cracked earth and pebbles along its bottom, 1 m high; (2) a newly dug irrigation channel with fresh earth banks and a thin stream of water in it, 0.8 m high; (3) a field of young green barley in rows, 0.5 m high; (4) ripe golden barley ready to cut, 1 m high.

Southern Mesopotamia c. 1750 BCE, the dry steppe west of the Euphrates and the farmland near Babylon: (1) a low half-built mud-brick house wall, 1.2 m high and 4 m long, bricks still drying beside it; (2) a small finished one-room mud-brick house with a flat reed-and-mud roof and a plain doorway, 2.6 m high; (3) a threshing floor of beaten earth with a heap of barley straw and grain, 0.8 m high.
